pr_title: Fix StackTraceTests to work with JIT optimization
pr_body:
Disable optimization/inlining on methods that are expected to
remain on the stack.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/36585
pr_comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @tommcdon, @krwq
Notify danmosemsft if you want to be subscribed.

That one is, but I don't think that's the right one. This one is missing it:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/61733e21bbe965977827205639bf4b835b522494/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.StackTrace/tests/StackTraceTests.cs#L338
The fix is likely to add NoInlining to that ctor.

This raises an interesting question. In release builds / runs, are most of our tests (the tests themselves) running unoptimized because they're generally only executed once and thus they won't be promoted from tier 0?

@stephentoub That's my belief, which is worrisome (I've expressed this worry before; don't remember to whom). cc @AndyAyersMS 

I'm planning to add back JIT stress mode testing over libraries (including simply no-tiering mode) with https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/36486, but it's worth considering whether a more regular mode, e.g., libraries PR or CI, should do this as well.

review_comments: Why is the NoOptimization part needed?  (I see it's used on a bunch of others above.)
Don't know. I was only following the example of the others nearby.
